summary.headline: Astral Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21.4% to Rs 3,566 crore with EBITDA margin at 13.7%, while management guides to a stronger H2 and a plumbing EBITDA of about Rs 1,050 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 revenue was Rs 3,566 crore (up about 21% YoY per the consolidated line, with the call quoting 26% in places) and consolidated EBITDA was Rs 272 crore at a 13.7% margin. Plumbing volume grew 19.1% in Q2 and 10.1% in H1, and management says October 2026 was the best October in company history. Margins were squeezed in Q2 by high-cost inventory and lagged pass-through of polymer price increases, with adhesive India at 10-11% and paint at about -5% EBITDA. Management expects H2 to improve on price pass-through, PVC/CPVC price hikes taken in October, and a favourable CPVC mix.

financial_highlights.change: vs Rs 2,938 crore YoY, about 21% (call also cites 26% for the quarter)

financial_highlights.value: Rs 6,700-ish crore not stated; plumbing H1 Rs 2,448 crore, adhesive India Rs 708 crore, adhesive UK Rs 247 crore, paint Rs 162 crore
financial_highlights.change: plumbing +18%, adhesive India +25%, adhesive UK +28%, paint +51% YoY

financial_highlights.value: Revenue Rs 53 million, EBITDA Rs 8 million
Inventory days 55-60 normal; Sept 30 snapshot elevated
financial_highlights.change: payable days reduced as management paid dollar liabilities early

segments.name: Plumbing
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 1,398 crore (+25%), EBITDA Rs 227 crore (16.3%); H1 EBITDA Rs 426 crore (17.4%). Management targets about Rs 1,050 crore plumbing EBITDA for FY27 and guides for double-digit volume growth.

segments.name: Adhesive India
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 382 crore (+25.3%), EBITDA about 11%, below the 14-15% guidance; management expects about 13-14% by year end and raised volume growth expectations above the earlier 15-20%.

segments.name: Adhesive UK
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 126 crore (+30%), EBITDA Rs 7.9 crore (6.3%); target 9-10% margin by year end, with new products (PEX, aluminium PEX, PPR, HDPE, electrofusion) expected to add from Q3.

segments.name: Paint (Pain)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 82 crore (+43.9%), EBITDA about -5% (Rs -4 crore); management targets 3-4% EBITDA by year end and 8-10% next year, and is pausing new geographies until margins reach 9-10%.

segments.name: DSS (specialty chemicals)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 53 million and EBITDA Rs 8 million; expansion planned to be ready by year end to scale products and backward-integrate adhesive and paint.

guidance_outlook: Plumbing FY27 EBITDA of about Rs 1,050 crore (management also cited Rs 1,250 crore consolidated, including about Rs 200 crore from chemicals); plumbing volume target about 290,000 tonnes (as per analyst math).
FY27 consolidated margin expected within 13-15%, with the company targeting a return to 15% by year end.
Adhesive India: growth expected to be well above the earlier 15-20% range; margin targeted at 13-14% by year end, then 14-15% normal.
Adhesive UK: 9-10% EBITDA margin target and 30% top-line run rate; paint EBITDA targeted at 3-4% by year end and 8-10% in FY28.

Capex for FY27 about Rs 400 crore (Rs 260 crore in H1), with around Rs 50-52 crore expected from sale of a Bangalore warehouse and office; CPVC backward-integration plant trials in the first month of Q4 and commercial readiness by the last month of Q4.
capex_capacity: Plastic plumbing capacity about 425 KT (per company; analyst cited 500 KT).
Management says land and buildings are in place to add about 100 KT in 6-9 months, with capex mainly for machinery.
CPVC backward-integration plant under construction, nearly complete with machinery being installed; ramp-up to full capacity in about one quarter after commissioning.
Aluminium PEX line installed and stabilised; commercial sales from own plant expected in Q3 FY27.
demand_pricing: October 2026 described as the best October in company history, with plumbing demand unprecedented; management expects double-digit momentum in Q3 and Q4.
Management says volume growth was a mix of market demand and share gains in geographies where Astral was weak; volume and value growth were broadly matched.
Price increases: PVC increases taken through October; CPVC price hiked about 5% in October; management says most cost inflation has been passed through.
Polymer MIP implemented, which management says sets a minimum base price around Rs 85-90 per kg; anti-dumping duty also cited as positive for the industry.
Management said Q2 pipe mix was skewed toward PVC pipes, because distributors bought pipes during a September scheme, which depressed CPVC fittings sales.

qa_highlights.question: Can plumbing growth reach 10-13% for FY27 given the high base in Q4 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said October was unprecedented and it targets volume of about 290,000 to 310,000 tonnes for the full year; it did not commit to a specific growth percentage.

qa_highlights.question: Why did inventory days and payable days move, and what are the PVC/CPVC holding costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days are normally 55-60; the Sept 30 figure was elevated by high-cost inventory. Payable days fell because management chose to pay dollar liabilities early to avoid forex risk, and it expects payable days to return to normal once currency stabilises.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q2 margin lower than Q1 in plumbing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed aggressive pricing to hit double-digit growth, lagged pass-through, and a September scheme that skewed distributors toward pipes over fittings. It said the H2 mix (CPVC and value-added products) is favourable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Capex for FY27 and what is the CPVC plant timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 capex was about Rs 260 crore; FY27 total is about Rs 400 crore after excluding goodwill, including Rs 40 crore for CPVC. CPVC commercial readiness is expected by the last month of Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for paint and UK margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Paint EBITDA is expected to be 3-4% by year end and 8-10% next year. UK is targeting 9-10% margin, up from 6.3% in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA trajectory for FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 10-15% EBITDA growth is achievable next year, and that operating costs should decline as a percentage of sales as absorption improves.

risks_watch: Polymer and crude price volatility from the war-related supply disruption; management says the lag in pass-through is a margin risk.
Adhesive India margins (11.5% H1) and UK (5.6% H1) are well below guidance and depend on pass-through.
Paint EBITDA is negative in Q2 and the business is still integrating legacy issues from the Gem acquisition.
Payable days have fallen and may return to normal, which could affect working capital.
Q2 volume and margin numbers were boosted by a one-off October surge; investors should watch whether H2 margins show the stated improvement.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and H2 recovery, with specific numerical targets, but evasive on exact growth percentages and margin bridges. Management acknowledged H1 margin pressure in adhesives, UK and paint and repeatedly asked investors to judge on a full-year basis.
key_quotes: we are very much conscious about bringing this abit margin back to the normal level in this quarter
we are highly confident that in the second half also we will be delivering much better number than what we have delivered in the first half.

adds.what: CPVC backward-integration plant (under construction, machinery being installed; ramp-up to full capacity about one quarter after commissioning)
Aluminium PEX line (installed and stabilised; commercial sales from own plant expected Q3 FY27)
About 100 KT plastic plumbing capacity addition (land and buildings in place; capex mainly machinery)

growth.why: Management guides double-digit plumbing volume growth (H1 10.1%), plumbing EBITDA ~Rs 1,050 crore and consolidated margin 13-15% rising to 15%, backed by PVC/CPVC price hikes, a ~100 KT capacity addition needing machinery and new CPVC/aluminium PEX lines, but no hard order numbers and the brief's revenue growth figures conflict (21% vs 26%).

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Consolidated margin 13.7% in Q2 with H1 at 14.5%, guided to 13-15% for FY27 and a return to 15% by year end; plumbing H1 margin 17.4% vs 16-18% guide, helped by PVC/CPVC price hikes taken in October and lagged polymer pass-through.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.when: Q2-Q3 FY28 window (about 100 KT in 6-9 months)
rows.why: Plastic plumbing capacity about 425 KT with land and buildings in place for a ~100 KT addition in 6-9 months (machinery capex only), plus CPVC backward-integration plant nearly complete with commercial readiness by last month of Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Plumbing volume grew 19.1% in Q2 and 10.1% in H1, October 2026 was the best October in company history, and management guides double-digit volume growth with a 290,000-310,000 tonne full-year target.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex about Rs 400 crore with Rs 260 crore spent in H1, and utilisation is rising, but no new capex beyond the existing plan (100 KT, CPVC, DSS expansion) was explicitly announced.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said October was unprecedented and sees double-digit momentum in Q3 and Q4, but it did not commit to a specific growth percentage and the Adhesive India guide was cut.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Adhesive India H1 margin of 11.5% is 2.5 points short of the 14-15% guide, UK at 5.6% H1 and paint at -5% in Q2 depend on pass-through, and polymer/crude volatility is a risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Aluminium PEX line installed and stabilised with commercial sales from own plant expected in Q3 FY27, and UK new products (PEX, aluminium PEX, PPR, HDPE, electrofusion) to add from Q3.

rows.label: Paint EBITDA to 3-4% by year end
rows.why: Paint EBITDA was about -5% (Rs -4 crore) on Rs 82 crore revenue in Q2, with management targeting 3-4% by year end and 8-10% in FY28, though new geographies are paused until margins reach 9-10%.

rows.label: Operating cost leverage in FY28
rows.why: Management said 10-15% EBITDA growth is achievable next year and operating costs should fall as a share of sales as absorption improves.

rows.label: Payable days normalisation
rows.why: Payable days fell as dollar liabilities were paid early to avoid forex risk, and management expects them to return to normal once currency stabilises, while inventory days (55-60 normal) were elevated on Sept 30.

tone.note: Management was confident on plumbing volume, October demand, and H2 price pass-through, but cautious on adhesive and paint margins and evasive on exact growth percentages; analysts pushed on the high Q4 FY26 base and the margin bridge.
